thread:
Ava (Product): FYI I uploaded the empirical bench gap analysis from last sprint — link: https://redwood-internal/drive/bench-gap-23 (summary below). Wanted to surface where onboarding acceptance criteria are failing and discuss tradeoffs for pin/deprecation windows.
Rory (Eng Runtime): skimmed it. tl;dr: long-context generation P95 latency is ~420ms on dedicated pools vs target 300ms. Small models ok.
Jin (ML): quality-wise, when we apply 4-bit quant to the candidate v2 there is a 2.8% drop on the eval set for multi-turn coherence (measured by our eval harness).
Ava (Product): key ask: can we get a short list of mitigations + rough effort so we can reframe onboarding gates? Customers waiting on this model.
Rory (Eng Runtime): immediate mitigations: 1) bump batch window for long-context by 10ms (low risk, minimal perf uplift). 2) enable KV prefetch for canaries (medium risk, needs infra change). 3) schedule a kernel swap for attention matmul for the v2 arch (high effort, high impact).
Jin (ML): also note that prompt formatting changes (trimming system prefaces) reduced mean tokens by 12% in trials — could help latency without model change.
Sam (Solutions): for customer cohorts, propose a staggered opt-in: early access (beta) with usage credits and SLA leniency, then full pin after 4 weeks or after meeting benchmarks. That buys us time to implement kernel swap.
Nora (Customer Ops): we have two enterprise customers on the fence. They asked for P95 < 350ms for long-context. They might accept a soft pin with rollback guarantees.
Ava (Product): proposed acceptance thresholds (draft): P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 350ms for long-context; quality delta <= 1.5% vs baseline on coh_eval. If not met, require compat shim + 8-week deprecation runway. Thoughts?
Rory (Eng Runtime): thresholds look reasonable. Need to add a canary checklist: perf run on dedicated pool, end-to-end integration test, cold-start measurement, and KV cache warmup verification.
Jin (ML): also require an eval slice for instruction-following regressions + a script to diff logits distribution. I can add a quick check.
CI Bot: perf-suite finished: dedicated-v2 long-context P95 = 422ms; P50 = 135ms; error rate 0.2%. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/perf/1713182023
Ava (Product): thanks. Action items: Rory to estimate effort for kernel swap + KV prefetch; Jin to add eval slice and run quantization sensitivity tests; Sam + Nora to draft customer opt-in comms and incentives. We should pick a canary cohort (<=5% traffic) and a 2-week staggered ramp.
Rory (Eng Runtime): will do. Quick ETA: KV prefetch 1-2 days prototype, kernel swap ~~2-3 sprints including perf validation.
Jin (ML): quant sensitivity tests scheduled today. Will post results in this thread.
Sam (Solutions): drafting comms now. Suggest offering 2 months of credits + dedicated support during the beta.
Ava (Product): ok lets reconvene Thu 11am to decide pin/ttl and soft-deprecation language. If the kernel swap is high-risk, we still need a fallback plan (auto-roll back to previous variant).
Rory (Eng Runtime): agree — will add automated rollback policy to the rollout playbook.
Jin (ML): posted quant test quick findings: 4-bit q reduces coherence score by 2.8, 8-bit q reduces by 0.9. Attaching snippet:
```
# run: python bench/quant_sens.py --model candidate-v2 --slices multi_turn,inst_follow
# output: coherence_drop: {"4bit": 2.8, "8bit": 0.9}
```
Sam (Solutions): noted. If 8-bit meets the quality bar, propose we ship 8-bit in dedicated and offer 4-bit as a cost-optional variant later.
Ava (Product): good trade. Final note: we need clear messaging in the catalog entry: pin status, known perf deltas, recommended usage (short vs long context), and migration instructions. Nora to own catalog copy.
Nora (Customer Ops): will draft catalog blurb and customer-facing FAQ by EOD Fri.
Ava (Product): great — marking this thread as the canonical gap-analysis discussion. Will add to the roadmap doc after Thu sync. :thumbsup:
